443. Control of civil aviation including the administration of the Aeronautics Act and regulations issued thereunder, $2,557,538.

I should like to bring to the attention of the minister the fact that all the members from the lower mainland of British Columbia have been very interested in getting the light airplanes off the international airport and over to the Boundary bay airport, in view of the fact that there are so many heavy aircraft and jets going into Vancouver now. I hope the minister will get the appropriate officials to make up their minds just where they are going to move so that we can avoid a major accident resulting from light airplanes interfering with the operation of the jets that are coming into the international airport. This condition has existed now for several years, but we have not been able to convince either the Department of Transport or the Department of National Defence to vacate the Boundary bay airport and make it available for the use of light planes. I would hope the minister would get the appropriate officials to make up their minds before there is a serious accident at Vancouver's international airport.

This item deals with the control of civil aviation. It seems to me that all across the country there is increasing concern about the consequent expenses in connection with rescues made necessary as a result of lost civil aircraft, particularly small aircraft. I am wondering if there has been a substantial tightening up of the penalties when it is found, after a rescue, that common sense has not been used by the pilot or perhaps even a failure to observe the regulations on which his licence is based. 1 know it is often found that planes have not carried radios. Sometimes even the department's advice on the colouring of aircraft has been disregarded and this has made it very difficult for the search planes to find lost aircraft. Sometimes flight plans have not been registered at all. In consequence millions of dollars are spent by the public, through the department of defence, the department of civil aviation and indeed by private air companies who can ill afford these sums in connection with these humane efforts to rescue people who have made their rescue difficult by flagrant violations of the laws on which their licences are based.
We do everything we can to try to get people to observe safety regulations and to use common sense. All I can say is that we will continue to try.

Are licences cancelled
when it is found, after rescue, that a flight

Supply-Transport
plan was not filed which could have been filed or that the airplane was not painted in accordance with the advice of the department?
I am advised by my officials that they cannot remember any particular instance, but if such occurrences do take place we would certainly take punitive action.

I hope the minister will permit me to say two or three words on this item. The minister will recall that last year and in 1958 the hon. member for Chicoutimi, with whom I am in full agreement for a change, spoke about the possibility of the establishment of an airport at St. Honore, which is close to Chicoutimi. This is not in my riding. I spoke to the minister privately about this matter lately. I also spoke to the hon. member for Chicoutimi. There is an area there containing nearly 100,000 people, many of whom are owners of private aircraft, who are deeply interested in civil aviation. I know the department has always stated they like to encourage civil aviation wherever it is possible. I know, too, that there are some regulations governing the establishment of airports across the country. I wonder if the minister and his officials would not send some representative to Chicoutimi or Jonquiere in my riding to study the situation and ascertain if there is something the department could do to remedy the situation.
Yes, I shall be glad to see that that is done.

speechtext:
This is a vote for a tremendous amount of money, $52 million for the construction or acquisition of buildings, works, land and equipment, including construction work on municipal airports and the like. I think the committee is entitled to some break-down of this large sum. I know that the minister, when he introduced his estimates, made a statement to which he
[Mr. Benidickson.j
attached a list, which I have before me, of votes in connection with air services and civil aviation. Is there a final estimate of the cost of the Montreal airport? The one I mentioned earlier was $30 million. Has that been increased because of the aeroquays that are being constructed in and around the building, on both sides, east and west of it?

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext: Can the minister give some indication, since the airport is likely to be completed before the end of I960, what his officers think the increase over $30 million is likely to be?
It could increase by up to $1 million.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext: I am sorry but I did not hear the minister's answer.
It could increase by up to $1 million, I am advised. We will not know until the final accounts.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext: Can I get some indication of what the position is at Malton? What is the estimate now? How far has it progressed? How many contracts have been awarded? When will it be completed?

The estimate for Malton at the present time is approximately the same as that for Dorval, namely about $30 million for stage one. That is the building and all related facilities that are planned at the present time. The first two contracts have been let for the foundation and field work. As to the third contract, the tender call will be made later this year. The terminal aeroquay will cost somewhere between $12 million and $15 million and the remainder of the $30 million is for the associated facilities.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext: How many more contracts will be required for Malton and what is the completion date at this time?
There will be one or more only for the terminal building but there will be four or live for runway paving and things of that kind and heating.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext: What is the completion date?
The target date is 1964; by 1964 or sooner, if possible.

Speaking to item 446, may I say that we are moving into the jet age and that it is a happy coincidence that we have a jet minister to go with this particular age. The minister has an extremely difficult department to administer. It is now possible to step into an airplane in Toronto and be in Vancouver in something slightly over four hours. What a tremendous transformation this is from the days of the DC-3's, the days of the milk run across western Canada, from the days of the nine, ten, eleven or twelve hours from Ottawa to Vancouver.
My only purpose in rising to speak on this item is to express the hope that, in the development of the jet stage of transportation in Canada we will not forget the inland airports. I am speaking, of course, for my own constituency, but I could speak for several others. There is a situation that is climatic. There is a climatic hazard in air travel in Canada. My own city of Medicine Hat had an all-time record in the war period of free flying days. There has been occasion after occasion when planes directed to other airports have been forced to land in the city of Medicine Hat because this was the only place at which they could get down. I hope that under this item there will be due recognition of the need, not only for maintaining, but possibly extending the runways, in order to take care of the faster planes and the larger planes, and extending the runways in order that we would at least have between Winnipeg and Vancouver one sound haven in the event of emergency. I am not pleading for our local traffic; our local traffic takes care of itself. We go to Regina; we go to Calgary and we go to Lethbridge. But certainly there is a need for the preservation of a completely safe haven for the larger planes in the event of extremely bad weather. I am suggesting that this subject should be given consideration by the minister.

I want to bring one item to the attention of the minister. I know the minister is quite aware of what I am going to say. It has to do with the Vancouver airport. The Vancouver city council has agreed to put up to the ratepayers of the Vancouver area the question of the sale of the airport to the Department of Transport to be operated as an international airport and this despite the fact that a previous sale had been voted down in a previous plebiscite because of the
Supply-Transport
short-sightedness of the previous government. There was first a token offer of one dollar; then there was an offer by the hon. member for Laurier, then minister of transport, of $500,000; then an offer by Mr. Campney of $1 million. That was the last offer.
I am suggesting to the minister that any offer made to the city of Vancouver must be based on the present value of the buildings and land and this offer must be on a fair basis which can be substantiated and which the people of Vancouver will recognize as being a fair and just offer. On that basis the city of Vancouver will vote for the sale of this airport but on any other basis they will not do so. It is absolutely essential that these factors be determined as soon as possible because it will take eighteen months to prepare plans and two years for construction, or a total of three and a half years for completion if started today.
The building is being used to capacity today. I hope that come December the Department of Transport will have something, such as a prospectus to put before the people of Vancouver, in order to show them what you are going to build there if they will turn the airport over to the Department of Transport. This is one of the most vital items that is coming up this year or next year as far as the Department of Transport is concerned. It is of major importance and I hope that action is taken immediately along the lines I have indicated.

Can the minister tell us the total extent of the plans of the department in respect to the airport and its facilities at Frobisher Bay; the total estimated costs of all the work projected there for the next two, three or four-year period?
We do not have any future airport development plans for Frobisher but we may put in some buildings such as airport housing for staff and small terminal improvements.
Does the minister have any idea of the total cost of these proposed installations?
The major cost of the airport development has been borne by the United States air force.

I wonder if I could ask the minister this question in view of the answer he gave the hon. member for Trinity with regard to the airport at Frobisher Bay. He mentioned that the major portion of the money spent on the runway extension was paid for by the United States air force. Is this airport to be part of the S.A.C. base, or is it to be used by commercial aircraft? Where does the minister think he will get the money to operate it?
It is a Department of Transport civil airport but the United States air force has a refuelling base there.
Is the United States air force using the base at the present time, or will it be in the future?
As soon as the runway is completed it will be used by the United States air force.
Is the Mont Joli airport operating now?
Yes, it is.

A supplementary question with respect to Frobisher Bay. Is there an agreement between the Department of Transport and the United States air force regarding facilities installed there by the United States air force and their acquisition by the Canadian government at the end of the period for which it will be useful for S.A.C.?
There is an intergovernmental agreement between the Canadian government and the United States government.
Does the minister know offhand what the general terms of that agreement are?

I am advised that these arrangements have been entered into by the Department of External Affairs and the state department of the United States and were comparable to the arrangement entered into with regard to bases used by the United States in Canada.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Liberal Party House Leader

Everybody got one at the beginning and I will send one over.

It would be repairs to the existing runway.
